title: Bridesmaids Tradition and Where It Comes From
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
notes: NEW ARTICLE (not a refresh): no old page or redirect. Overlap: the live page /expert-advice/what-do-bridesmaids-wear (dress) and /trending/whats-inside-rei-germars-bridesmaid-kit (celebrity news) are cross-links, not competitors. The pillar draft (/expert-advice/wedding-traditions) has a short bridesmaids section with myth-busting wording: do not edit it; suggest a backlink only. SEO checks whether any site page ranks for the keyword.

AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Customs without a strong source are written as living practice in a confident voice ('Many couples...'), never with a meaning or origin stated as fact. 'Often told' at most once per post, never 'it is often told that'. No hedge stacking: cite a source once by link; date legal and travel facts once per section. Source gaps go in the run report only. No per-line source credits (never 'Britannica describes', 'the museum holds', 'the study records'). No myth-busting lines ('you will often read', 'confident dates').

Topic: the bridesmaid tradition. The title promises where it comes from: state an origin, date or meaning as fact ONLY where a fact gives it (never 'dressed alike to confuse evil spirits' unless a reference states it). Otherwise cover what bridesmaids do today, confidently: choosing them, roles, the maid or matron of honour, mixed-gender wedding parties, destination wedding logistics for the wedding party.

Likely sections (brief finalises): why we have bridesmaids today; early history as sourced (e.g. Roman or biblical references only as references give them); Victorian and royal bridesmaids (e.g. Queen Victoria's 12 bridesmaids, as the Royal Collection Trust or V&A describe them); maid or matron of honour; matching dresses as sourced; how many bridesmaids; roles before and on the day; mixed wedding parties (bridesmen); bridesmaids at a destination wedding (travel, who pays, as practical questions); thanking your bridesmaids.

Sources: V&A, Royal Collection Trust (rct.uk), royal.uk, Britannica, Oxford Reference (folklore dictionaries), academic dress-history sources, Smartraveller for travel lines. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs, bridal retailers or Wikipedia.
No travel or legal section (not a country article); no Smartraveller needed.

Links: /expert-advice/what-do-bridesmaids-wear, /trending/whats-inside-rei-germars-bridesmaid-kit once if natural, /expert-advice/why-do-brides-wear-veils, /expert-advice/something-old-something-new, the pillar /expert-advice/wedding-traditions, /wonderland-concierge, /magazine. UTMs: utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=why-do-we-have-bridesmaids&utm_content=primary|secondary.
Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people; AI only for a neutral still life (bridesmaid bouquets on linen) labelled illustrative pending approval; museum or royal images only if licensed.

Speed: Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: history and origins (early, Victorian, royal) and folklore meanings; B: roles today, maid or matron of honour, bridesmen, destination and travel), 15 min HARD by the clock, start no new reads after the limit, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence a number; must_include_coverage objects with covered_by arrays; never retry a declined call.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.
Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md; no Wedded Privileges or inclusions beyond brand facts.

Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or designer names; no amounts (who pays is written as questions); business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
